title: 1 Kings 17 — Eliyahu (Elijah) at the brook Kerit and the widow of Tzarfat

translation.sourceText: Hebrew Masoretic text (Westminster Leningrad Codex base, Public Domain) — Tanach with Ta'amei Hamikra

citations: Burney, Notes on the Hebrew Text of the Books of Kings (1903), ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed: mittōšāḇê (min + cstr. pl. of tôšāḇ) gilʿāḏ; ḥay-YHWH oath + ʾăšer ʿāmaḏtî ləp̄ānāyw; ʾim-yihyeh ... kî ʾim-ləp̄î dəḇārî. Disputed only in keeping the MT 'settlers' against LXX 'from Tishbe' adopted by NRSV; the MT is construable and the versional reading is recorded, which is the right MT-baseline call. 'Elohim of Yisra'el' per corpus convention; no lens.
wayəhî dəḇar-YHWH ʾēlāyw lēʾmōr rendered exactly by the formula convention.
lēḵ mizzeh ûp̄ānîṯā ləḵā qēḏmâ wənistartā bənaḥal kərîṯ ʾăšer ʿal-pənê hayyardēn: literal 'before the Yarden' = ASV; the 'east of' sense is correctly given in commentary.
wəʾeṯ-hāʿōrəḇîm ṣiwwîṯî ləḵalkelḵā: MT vocalization 'the ravens' with every ancient version; the 'Arabs' revocalization is rightly rejected. Line equals ASV; no lens.
Two wayyēleḵ clauses and wayyēšeḇ rendered; 'stayed' for yšb acceptable (ASV 'dwelt').

Participle məḇîʾîm rendered progressive 'were bringing'; LXX variant (bread morning / meat evening) correctly described. Reception note accurately reports TBWTT ch. 3 ('carrier ravens') and is labelled; the line adds nothing.
miqqēṣ yāmîm 'after some days'; kî lōʾ-hāyâ gešem 'because there had been no rain'. Exact.
Formula as 17:2.
qûm lēḵ ṣārəp̄aṯâ ʾăšer ləṣîḏôn; ʾiššâ ʾalmānâ 'a widow woman' is the literal apposition. Exact.
məqōšešeṯ ʿēṣîm 'gathering sticks'; qəḥî-nāʾ ... bakkəlî 'Please bring me ... in a vessel'. Exact.
wattēleḵ lāqaḥaṯ 'as she was going to bring it'; paṯ-leḥem 'a morsel of bread'. Exact.

Re-parsed oath ḥay-YHWH ʾĕlōheyḵā; ʾim-yeš-lî māʿôḡ (oath-negative 'I have no'); kî ʾim məlōʾ kap̄-qemaḥ bakkaḏ ... baṣṣappāḥaṯ; waʿăśîṯîhû ... waʾăḵalnuhû wāmāṯnû. Accurate; 'your Elohim' per convention.
ʾal-tîrʾî; bōʾî ʿăśî ḵiḏḇārēḵ; ʿugâ qəṭannâ bāriʾšōnâ ... bāʾaḥărōnâ. Exact.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed. 2012), on Ketiv/Qere
verdicts.reasoning: Ketiv/Qere verified in source: K tittēn / Q tēt; 'until the day that YHWH gives rain' renders the Qere (the sense is identical). 'upon the face of the ground' is more literal than ASV 'upon the earth' (ʾăḏāmâ). Approved.
Ketiv hwʾ-whyʾ / Qere hîʾ wāhûʾ verified; 'she and he' follows the Qere. Bare yāmîm 'for days' is kept without ASV's supplied '[many]' and the gloss is in commentary. Approved.
kad haqqemaḥ lōʾ ḵālāṯâ ... lōʾ ḥāsēr ... bəyaḏ ʾēliyyāhû 'through Eliyahu'. Exact.
ḥālâ ben-hāʾiššâ baʿălaṯ habbāyiṯ; ʿaḏ ʾăšer lōʾ-nôṯərâ-bô nəšāmâ 'until there was no breath left in him'. Exact; the commentary correctly notes the text does not state death explicitly.

Disputed only in 'man of the Elohim': the MT has the article (ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm), and following it is grammatically exact under the corpus decision not to translate ʾĕlōhîm. mah-llî wālāḵ and ləhazkîr ʾeṯ-ʿăwōnî correctly rendered.
tənî-lî ʾeṯ-bənēḵ; mēḥêqāh 'from her bosom'; hāʿălîyâ 'the upper chamber'. Exact.
hăḡam ʿal-hāʾalmānâ ... hărēʿôṯā ləhāmîṯ ʾeṯ-bənāh: question with infinitive of result, rendered as ASV. Exact.

citations: Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament (1974)
verdicts.reasoning: wayyiṯmōḏēḏ (hithpael mdd) 'stretched himself'; tāšāḇ nāʾ nep̄eš-hayyeleḏ hazzeh ʿal-qirbô. Transliterated 'nefesh' (changed from draft 'nephesh' for spelling only) is defensible where the noun names the life that returns, and avoids ASV's dualist 'soul'; governed by central tzet-nephesh. No lens.
wayyišmaʿ YHWH bəqôl ʾēliyyāhû; wattāšāḇ nep̄eš-hayyeleḏ ʿal-qirbô wayyeḥî: exact echo of v 21 kept. Approved.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ הַתִּשְׁבִּ֜י מִתֹּשָׁבֵ֣י גִלְעָד֮ אֶל־אַחְאָב֒ חַי־יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָמַ֣דְתִּי לְפָנָ֔יו אִם־יִהְיֶ֛ה הַשָּׁנִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה טַ֣ל וּמָטָ֑ר כִּ֖י אִם־לְפִ֥י דְבָרִֽי׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And Eliyahu the Tishbite, of the settlers of Gil'ad, said to Ach'av, "As YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el, lives, before whom I stand, there shall be neither dew nor rain these years, except by my word."

notes.official:
*mittōšāḇê gilʿāḏ* 'of the settlers of Gil'ad' follows the MT vocalization (*tōšāḇ* 'resident, settler'; ASV 'of the sojourners of Gilead'). The LXX reads *ek Thesbōn tēs Galaad* 'from Tishbe of Gilead', i.e. *mittišbê*, which pairs with *hattišbî* 'the Tishbite' and is adopted by NRSV and many commentators (Burney 1903; Cogan, *1 Kings*, AB 10, 2001); the MT is construable, so it is kept and the versional reading recorded (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

Names: Eliyahu = Elijah, Ach'av = Ahab, Gil'ad = Gilead, Yisra'el = Israel (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`). The prophet's name, 'my El is Yah', anticipates the confession of 18:39.

*ḥay-YHWH ... ʾăšer ʿāmaḏtî ləp̄ānāyw* 'As YHWH ... lives, before whom I stand': the Israelite oath formula (`chei-x-oath-by-the-life-formula`) with the courtier's idiom 'stand before' = serve. *ṭal ûmāṭār* 'dew and rain' names both sources of moisture in the Levantine dry and wet seasons; the drought is aimed at the domain claimed for the storm god Ba'al (Cogan; Smith, *The Early History of God*, 2002).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֥יו לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And the word of YHWH came to him, saying,

paragraphs.text: לֵ֣ךְ מִזֶּ֔ה וּפָנִ֥יתָ לְּךָ֖ קֵ֑דְמָה וְנִסְתַּרְתָּ֙ בְּנַ֣חַל כְּרִ֔ית אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: "Go from here and turn eastward, and hide yourself by the brook Kerit, which is before the Yarden.

notes.official: *ʿal-pənê hayyardēn* (vv 3, 5): ASV 'before the Jordan'. Because Hebrew orientation faces east, *ʿal-pənê* 'in front of' often means 'east of' (BDB *pānîm* II.7; cf. Gen 23:19; 25:18), and NRSV/NJPS translate 'east of the Jordan'. The literal 'before' is kept; the geographical sense is given here. Kerit = Cherith, Yarden = Jordan.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֖ה מֵהַנַּ֣חַל תִּשְׁתֶּ֑ה וְאֶת־הָעֹרְבִ֣ים צִוִּ֔יתִי לְכַלְכֶּלְךָ֖ שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: And it shall be that you shall drink from the brook; and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there."

notes.official: *hāʿōrəḇîm* 'the ravens' (vv 4, 6) follows the MT vocalization, the LXX (*korakes*), the Vulgate and the Targum (`orvim-ravens-mt-vocalization-1-kings-17`; lexeme as in `yonah-orev`). The consonants *ʿrbym* also allow *ʿarḇîm* 'Arabs', and a rabbinic tradition (Genesis Rabbah 33:5) took them as people of a town; neither reading has textual support. *ṣiwwîṯî ləḵalkelḵā* 'I have commanded ... to feed you' recurs with the widow in v 9: YHWH commands both the birds and the foreign woman to sustain the prophet.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ וַיַּ֖עַשׂ כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ וַיֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ בְּנַ֣חַל כְּרִ֔ית אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: So he went and did according to the word of YHWH; he went and stayed by the brook Kerit, which is before the Yarden.

paragraphs.text: וְהָעֹרְבִ֗ים מְבִיאִ֨ים ל֜וֹ לֶ֤חֶם וּבָשָׂר֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְלֶ֥חֶם וּבָשָׂ֖ר בָּעָ֑רֶב וּמִן־הַנַּ֖חַל יִשְׁתֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And the ravens were bringing him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the brook.

notes.official:
The participle *məḇîʾîm* 'were bringing' describes a regular, repeated supply, morning and evening, like the manna and quail of Ex 16:8, 12. The LXX reads 'bread in the morning and meat in the evening', closer still to Ex 16; the MT has bread and meat at both times.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) cites this verse as an example of the Elohim provisioning Eliyahu discreetly, by 'carrier ravens'. That reading takes the MT 'ravens' as it stands; the translation adds nothing to the line.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֛י מִקֵּ֥ץ יָמִ֖ים וַיִּיבַ֣שׁ הַנָּ֑חַל כִּ֛י לֹֽא־הָיָ֥ה גֶ֖שֶׁם בָּאָֽרֶץ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And it came to pass after some days that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֥יו לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And the word of YHWH came to him, saying,

paragraphs.text: ק֣וּם לֵ֤ךְ צָרְפַ֙תָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְצִיד֔וֹן וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֖ שָׁ֑ם הִנֵּ֨ה צִוִּ֥יתִי שָׁ֛ם אִשָּׁ֥ה אַלְמָנָ֖ה לְכַלְכְּלֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: "Arise, go to Tzarfat, which belongs to Tzidon, and stay there; behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain you."

notes.official: Tzarfat = Zarephath, a Phoenician coastal town between Tyre and Sidon (Tzidon): the prophet of YHWH is sent into the home territory of Izevel's father, Ethbaal king of the Sidonians (16:31). Luke 4:25-26 recalls the episode.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣קָם ׀ וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ צָרְפַ֗תָה וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־פֶּ֣תַח הָעִ֔יר וְהִנֵּֽה־שָׁ֛ם אִשָּׁ֥ה אַלְמָנָ֖ה מְקֹשֶׁ֣שֶׁת עֵצִ֑ים וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר קְחִי־נָ֨א לִ֧י מְעַט־מַ֛יִם בַּכְּלִ֖י וְאֶשְׁתֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: So he arose and went to Tzarfat; and when he came to the gate of the city, behold, a widow woman was there gathering sticks. And he called to her and said, "Please bring me a little water in a vessel, that I may drink."

paragraphs.text: וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ לָקַ֑חַת וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר לִֽקְחִי־נָ֥א לִ֛י פַּת־לֶ֖חֶם בְּיָדֵֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And as she was going to bring it, he called to her and said, "Please bring me a morsel of bread in your hand."

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר חַי־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ אִם־יֶשׁ־לִ֣י מָע֔וֹג כִּ֣י אִם־מְלֹ֤א כַף־קֶ֙מַח֙ בַּכַּ֔ד וּמְעַט־שֶׁ֖מֶן בַּצַּפָּ֑חַת וְהִנְנִ֨י מְקֹשֶׁ֜שֶׁת שְׁנַ֣יִם עֵצִ֗ים וּבָ֙אתִי֙ וַעֲשִׂיתִ֙יהוּ֙ לִ֣י וְלִבְנִ֔י וַאֲכַלְנֻ֖הוּ וָמָֽתְנוּ׃

i18n.en: And she said, "As YHWH your Elohim lives, I have no baked cake, only a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the jug; and behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and prepare it for me and for my son, that we may eat it and die."

notes.official: *ḥay-YHWH ʾĕlōheyḵā* 'As YHWH your Elohim lives': the Phoenician widow swears by Eliyahu's god, 'your Elohim' (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, construct with possessor). *māʿôḡ* 'baked cake' is a rare word (also Ps 35:16).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלֶ֤יהָ אֵלִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אַל־תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י בֹּ֖אִי עֲשִׂ֣י כִדְבָרֵ֑ךְ אַ֣ךְ עֲשִׂי־לִ֣י מִ֠שָּׁם עֻגָ֨ה קְטַנָּ֤ה בָרִאשֹׁנָה֙ וְהוֹצֵ֣אתְ לִ֔י וְלָ֣ךְ וְלִבְנֵ֔ךְ תַּעֲשִׂ֖י בָּאַחֲרֹנָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And Eliyahu said to her, "Do not fear. Go, do as you have said; but first make me a little cake from it and bring it out to me, and afterward make some for yourself and for your son.

notes.official: *ʾal-tîrʾî* 'Do not fear' (`al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula`), here in a prophet's mouth before the oracle of v 14.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י כֹה֩ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כַּ֤ד הַקֶּ֙מַח֙ לֹ֣א תִכְלָ֔ה וְצַפַּ֥חַת הַשֶּׁ֖מֶן לֹ֣א תֶחְסָ֑ר עַ֠ד י֧וֹם תתן־[תֵּת־] יְהוָ֛ה גֶּ֖שֶׁם עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: For thus says YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el: 'The jar of flour shall not be used up, and the jug of oil shall not run short, until the day that YHWH gives rain upon the face of the ground.'"

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *tittēn* (finite, 'YHWH gives') / Qere *tēt* (infinitive construct, 'the giving of'); the Qere is translated ('until the day that YHWH gives rain'), with the same sense (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). *ʿal-pənê hāʾăḏāmâ* 'upon the face of the ground' (`adam-adamah`).

paragraphs.text: וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ וַתַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה כִּדְבַ֣ר אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ וַתֹּ֧אכַל הוא־והיא [הִֽיא־] [וָה֛וּא] וּבֵיתָ֖הּ יָמִֽים׃

i18n.en: And she went and did according to the word of Eliyahu; and she and he and her household ate for days.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *hûʾ-wəhîʾ* 'he and she' / Qere *hîʾ wāhûʾ* 'she and he'; the Qere, which puts the widow first, is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). *yāmîm* 'days' stands alone; ASV supplies '[many] days', NJPS 'for a long time'. The translation keeps the bare 'for days'.

paragraphs.text: כַּ֤ד הַקֶּ֙מַח֙ לֹ֣א כָלָ֔תָה וְצַפַּ֥חַת הַשֶּׁ֖מֶן לֹ֣א חָסֵ֑ר כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר בְּיַ֥ד אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: The jar of flour was not used up, and the jug of oil did not run short, according to the word of YHWH which he spoke through Eliyahu.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה חָלָ֕ה בֶּן־הָאִשָּׁ֖ה בַּעֲלַ֣ת הַבָּ֑יִת וַיְהִ֤י חָלְיוֹ֙ חָזָ֣ק מְאֹ֔ד עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־נֽוֹתְרָה־בּ֖וֹ נְשָׁמָֽה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass after these things that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick; and his sickness was very severe, until there was no breath left in him.

notes.official: *ʿaḏ ʾăšer lōʾ-nôṯərâ-bô nəšāmâ* 'until there was no breath left in him': *nəšāmâ* is the breath of life (Gen 2:7). The text does not say outright that the boy died; the mother's words (v 18), Eliyahu's prayer (v 20) and the 'return' of the *nefesh* (vv 21-22) show that the narrator treats him as dead (Cogan, *1 Kings*).

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ מַה־לִּ֥י וָלָ֖ךְ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים בָּ֧אתָ אֵלַ֛י לְהַזְכִּ֥יר אֶת־עֲוֺנִ֖י וּלְהָמִ֥ית אֶת־בְּנִֽי׃

i18n.en: And she said to Eliyahu, "What have I to do with you, O man of the Elohim? Have you come to me to bring my iniquity to remembrance and to kill my son?"

notes.official: *ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm* 'man of the Elohim' (ASV 'man of God'): the prophetic title, rendered following the Hebrew article (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`). *mah-llî wālāḵ* 'What have I to do with you?' is a formula of protest that distances the speaker from the addressee (Judg 11:12; 2 Sam 16:10). The widow assumes that the holy man's presence has drawn divine attention to her own sin (*ʿăwōnî*).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלֶ֖יהָ תְּנִֽי־לִ֣י אֶת־בְּנֵ֑ךְ וַיִּקָּחֵ֣הוּ מֵחֵיקָ֗הּ וַֽיַּעֲלֵ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־הָעֲלִיָּ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־הוּא֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב שָׁ֔ם וַיַּשְׁכִּבֵ֖הוּ עַל־מִטָּתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he said to her, "Give me your son." And he took him from her bosom and carried him up to the upper chamber where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.

notes.official: *hāʿălîyâ* 'the upper chamber' is a roof room, a mark of a well-to-do household (cf. 2 Kgs 4:10). This fits the description of the widow in v 17 as *baʿălaṯ habbayiṯ* 'the mistress of the house', though v 12 shows her near starvation.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י הֲ֠גַם עַל־הָאַלְמָנָ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֨י מִתְגּוֹרֵ֥ר עִמָּ֛הּ הֲרֵע֖וֹתָ לְהָמִ֥ית אֶת־בְּנָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And he called to YHWH and said, "O YHWH my Elohim, have you also brought evil upon the widow with whom I am sojourning, by killing her son?"

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתְמֹדֵ֤ד עַל־הַיֶּ֙לֶד֙ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ פְּעָמִ֔ים וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י תָּ֥שָׁב נָ֛א נֶֽפֶשׁ־הַיֶּ֥לֶד הַזֶּ֖ה עַל־קִרְבּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and called to YHWH and said, "O YHWH my Elohim, please let the nefesh of this child return into him."

notes.official:
*wayyiṯmōḏēḏ* 'and he stretched himself' (hithpael of *mdd* 'measure'): Eliyahu measures himself against the child three times; compare Elisha's fuller version of the act in 2 Kgs 4:34-35.

*tāšāḇ-nāʾ nep̄eš-hayyeleḏ hazzeh ʿal-qirbô* 'let the nefesh of this child return into him': here *nepeš* names the life that has left the body and returns 'into his inward part', so it is transliterated per the central `tzet-nephesh-departure-at-death-formula`, which reads these verses as the return-counterpart of Gen 35:18 (*bəṣēʾṯ napšāh* 'as her nefesh was departing'). ASV 'soul' carries a dualist sense the Hebrew does not require (HALOT *nepeš*; Wolff, *Anthropology of the Old Testament*, 1974). Spelling 'nefesh' per `nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה בְּק֣וֹל אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ וַתָּ֧שָׁב נֶֽפֶשׁ־הַיֶּ֛לֶד עַל־קִרְבּ֖וֹ וַיֶּֽחִי׃

i18n.en: And YHWH listened to the voice of Eliyahu; and the nefesh of the child returned into him, and he lived.

notes.official: *wattāšāḇ nep̄eš-hayyeleḏ ʿal-qirbô wayyeḥî* 'and the nefesh of the child returned into him, and he lived' fulfils the petition of v 21 word for word (`tzet-nephesh-departure-at-death-formula`; `nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ אֶת־הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַיֹּרִדֵ֤הוּ מִן־הָעֲלִיָּה֙ הַבַּ֔יְתָה וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖הוּ לְאִמּ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ רְאִ֖י חַ֥י בְּנֵֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu took the child and brought him down from the upper chamber into the house, and gave him to his mother; and Eliyahu said, "See, your son lives."

notes.official:
*rəʾî ḥay bənēḵ* 'See, your son lives' answers the oath *ḥay-YHWH* of 17:1, 12: the chapter is organized around *ḥay* 'living'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse and reads the revival as medical resuscitation of a dying child. The Hebrew does not specify a mechanism and the line does not supply one.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶל־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ עַתָּה֙ זֶ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ אֱלֹהִ֖ים אָ֑תָּה וּדְבַר־יְהוָ֥ה בְּפִ֖יךָ אֱמֶֽת׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And the woman said to Eliyahu, "Now by this I know that you are a man of Elohim, and that the word of YHWH in your mouth is truth."

notes.official: *ʾîš ʾĕlōhîm ʾattâ* 'you are a man of Elohim': anarthrous here, unlike the articular title of v 18, and rendered accordingly (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`); conventional English 'a man of God' (ASV, and the English edition of The Book Which Tells the Truth, ch. 3, which quotes the verse). *ûḏəḇar-YHWH bəp̄îḵā ʾĕmeṯ* 'the word of YHWH in your mouth is truth': the Phoenician widow's confession closes the chapter and anticipates the public confession of 18:39.
